sections.text: Audible Noise and Loosely Bolted Parts

items:
Listen 
 and check for any abnormal sounds from the main tank and accessories as a 
 rattling sound indicates loose bolts and a repetitive scraping sound indicates 
 worn fan or oil pump bearings.

Visually 
 inspect bolted connections in the transformer's main and auxiliary circuits, 
 foundation bolts and all other bolted connections to ensure that all parts are 
 secure.

Check for 
 leakage from the transformer tank, valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints welds 
 etc.

The 
 silica-gel absorbent inside the breather bottle is normally magenta blue, but 
 turns pink if excessive moisture is present, dry or replace the silica gel if 
 more than 70% is pink.

Check 
 that the sight-glass level of the sealing oil in the oil cup is between the 
 HIGH and LOW marks, it must be correct at all times because excessive sealing 
 oil in the cup may contaminate the silica-gel, while a shortage of oil may not 
 seal the conservator properly.

Check for 
 cracks, oil or gas leakage or any sign of damage to the pressure plate.

Check for 
 an excessive buildup of grime on the radiator surface and remove it.

Check 
 that any oil flow indicator installed in the system shows that oil is 
 circulating.

Check 
 that radiator valves are in the open position.

If the 
 bushings are equipped with an oil gauge, use binoculars to visually check the 
 oil level and for signs of leakage.

Check the 
 porcelain for cracking and other damage.

Check 
 that there is no overheating of the terminals; inspect the terminals for heat 
 discoloration using binoculars or infra red scope.

Check the 
 transformer's protective relays at the site control room and check that they 
 have not actuated.

Introduction
This document outlines the equipment inspection I1, which must be performed 
on monthly bases 
as indicated by M1 in the title block.
The first draft initiated by eng.
 Amr Gaber, revised by eng. Mohamed Abbas 
 Ahmad, tested by eng Mohammed El-bayaa, 
 accepted by general manager eng. Mohamed Abbas Ahmad, approved by eng. Mahmoud 
 El-Naquib head sector of Ayoun Moussa PS.
This document certified by eng. Mohamed Fayez 
Hassan EDEPC MPIS coordinator.
Safety 
Precautions
A work permit must be issued
The maintenance staff should carry the suitable ID safety category
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required
Wear the appropriate 
 safety equipment as safety shoes, helmet
Transformer must be out of service and isolated and grounded 
 from all sides.
Don't 
 go too close to energized areas on the transformer while it is operating too 
 close, means as a general understanding within a spherical area whose center 
 is the top of the bushing and whose radius is the full length from the top 
 of the bushing flange (ground potential) of the bushing.

Transformer Temperatures, Load and Voltages
Read oil 
 and winding temperature, check that the maximum temperatures are not being 
 exceeded, also check that the temperature is acceptable by comparing it with 
 past entries in the inspection log.
Voltages 
 and load must be kept within the specified limits, which are in the 
 instruction manual.
Oil Level
Read the 
 values on the oil level gauges, check that the oil level readings are correct 
 for the oil temperature, in compliance with the graph on the nameplate located 
 near them, (in nameplate) and this graph also appears in the transformers 
 instruction manual.
Audible Noise and Loosely Bolted Parts
Listen 
 and check for any abnormal sounds from the main tank and accessories as a 
 rattling sound indicates loose bolts and a repetitive scraping sound indicates 
 worn fan or oil pump bearings.
Loosely Bolted Parts
Visually 
 inspect bolted connections in the transformer's main and auxiliary circuits, 
 foundation bolts and all other bolted connections to ensure that all parts are 
 secure.
Oil Leakage
Check for 
 leakage from the transformer tank, valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints welds 
 etc.
Dehydrating Breather
The 
 silica-gel absorbent inside the breather bottle is normally magenta blue, but 
 turns pink if excessive moisture is present, dry or replace the silica gel if 
 more than 70% is pink.
Check 
 that the sight-glass level of the sealing oil in the oil cup is between the 
 HIGH and LOW marks, it must be correct at all times because excessive sealing 
 oil in the cup may contaminate the silica-gel, while a shortage of oil may not 
 seal the conservator properly.
Pressure Relief Device
Check for 
 cracks, oil or gas leakage or any sign of damage to the pressure plate.
Cooling Equipment
Check for 
 an excessive buildup of grime on the radiator surface and remove it.
Check 
 that any oil flow indicator installed in the system shows that oil is 
 circulating.
Check 
 that radiator valves are in the open position.
Bushings
If the 
 bushings are equipped with an oil gauge, use binoculars to visually check the 
 oil level and for signs of leakage.
Check the 
 porcelain for cracking and other damage.
Check 
 that there is no overheating of the terminals; inspect the terminals for heat 
 discoloration using binoculars or infra red scope.
Protective Relays
Check the 
 transformer's protective relays at the site control room and check that they 
 have not actuated.
